# Lab report reading benchmark

<!-- Generated by `npm run benchmark` (healthnet-frontend/src/benchmark/labBenchmark.test.js). Don't edit by hand. -->

**Test set:** 600 synthetic lab reports, seed 20261025 (`src/benchmark/synthLabReports.js`) · **Speed** (parsing only, on the machine that ran the benchmark; on-device OCR not included): rules 5.15 ms per report, rules + Tagger 5.29 ms

The documents are made up: random values in 6 real-world layouts, with look-alike tests (LDL, eAG, post-prandial glucose, ratios) that must not be read, header lines full of other numbers, and OCR-style noise on half of them. Test names and units are written independently of the parser's dictionary, so names it doesn't know count against it. None of the test names was in the Tagger's training data; the ones the rules can't place were kept out even inside longer names.

- **Correct** means the value is within the rounding of the printed number, with any required flag (plain "Glucose" must be flagged as possibly not fasting).
- **Dangerous error** means a wrong value that the review screen pre-ticks (in range, confidence ≥ 0.5), so one click would save it.

## Readers compared

| | Values | Precision | Recall | F1 | Dangerous error rate | Documents with a dangerous error |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rules only | 3809 | 99.7% | 87.0% | 92.9% | 0.0% | 0.0% |
| Rules + Tagger (shipped) | 3809 | 99.7% | 96.4% | 98.0% | 0.0% | 0.0% |
